outline: 1388 Mental Shortcuts for Adding and Subtracting Integers

examples.question_text:
Put $-17, \; 8, \; -3, \; 11, \; -9$ in:
(a) ascending order
(b) descending order.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Read from left to right on a number line, smallest to largest:
$-17, \; -9, \; -3, \; 8, \; 11$.
(b) Read from right to left, largest to smallest:
$11, \; 8, \; -3, \; -9, \; -17$.

examples.question_text: List all integers greater than $-26$ and less than $-19$, in ascending order.
examples.solution_text:
Do not include $-26$ or $-19$ because the comparisons are strict. Read the integers between them from left to right:
$-25, \; -24, \; -23, \; -22, \; -21, \; -20$.

examples.question_text:
Three lakes have altitudes of $-35$ m, $-120$ m and $-18$ m relative to sea level.
(a) Which altitude is greatest?
(b) Which lake is lowest?
examples.solution_text:
(a) Among negative integers, the one closest to zero is greatest. The greatest altitude is $-18$ m.
(b) The lowest altitude is the smallest integer:
$-120<-35<-18$.
The lake at $-120$ m is lowest.

examples.question_text: City A has a temperature of $-9^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and city B has a temperature of $-2^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. City C is warmer than city A but colder than city B. Give one possible integer temperature for city C.
